The claim's conditional is also true: ChromaAgentMemory.open_error is a getter-only @property (agent_memory.py:154-164), so assignment on a real one would raise AttributeError; the tests avoid that by using the stub.

results.evidence: The verify-memory runner (src/sqllens/eval/runner.py:131-138) calls query_database_impl_with_widgets. _run_one_case (runner.py:159-175) wraps the driver call in `except Exception`, so the AgentRunError for a memory-unavailable turn (raised in tools/query_database.py:759-763 with agent_trace/query_info, and at :719 with no kwargs) is caught. It is recorded as CaseResult(status=ERROR, error='AgentRunError: <msg>'). actual_sql uses _extract_sql(exc.query_info) when isinstance AgentRunError. AgentRunError.__init__ (query_database.py:63-71) always sets query_info (default None), and _extract_sql returns None for a non-dict. So it cannot crash with AttributeError.

agent_memory.py:154-164: open_error returns None if self._client is not None, else _open_error. _client is assigned only at :123 (init None) and :151 (success), never reset to None. So once any thread succeeds, a later failing thread (sets _open_error at :148) cannot make the property return non-None. Failing before the success also is overwritten by :150. Only a transient window between :150 and :151 exists, not a failure finishing after success.

src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:696-697 comment says a turn whose send_message raised left above with the internal error and only the unanswered-tool_use trim. The except chain around send_message (lines 641-689) has other exits: asyncio.CancelledError (660-671) does a full _rollback_conversation and re-raises CancelledError, with no internal error and no trim; UnsafeSqlError (672-679) and RlsError (680-683) raise RuntimeError(str(e)) with the guard message, not _INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE, and the trim at 650-655 runs only for Exception subclasses. Only the generic Exception branch (684-689) matches the comment. The absolute claim is false.

results.evidence: _MEMORY_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE (query_database.py:98-103) is a fixed literal with no interpolation. Both raise sites (query_database.py:719 with `from e`, and ~760) build AgentRunError from only that constant. The Chroma exception is logged server-side via logger.warning(exc_info=open_error) (~754). Client rendering uses only str(exc): server.py:387 _trace_error_result(str(exc),...) -> 'Error executing tool query_database: {message}' (server.py:182), and FastMCP's default path formats the message only. __cause__/__context__ (set by `from e` at 719) are not rendered into client text, so no chained leakage.

NORMALIZED (wording-only): src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:374-376 declares reason: str = "cancelled"; the cancellation caller (~668) passes 4 positional args and the memory-unavailable caller (~700) passes reason="memory-unavailable". All 5 format strings have matching placeholder/arg counts (3/3, 2/2, 3/3, 3/3, 3/3). However, 'keeps its log text' is not exact: git diff vs main shows the cancelled-path tails changed from 'the cancelled call's messages' to 'that call's messages' (two error strings), and the leading 'cancelled' became a %s that renders 'cancelled' (same lowercase). So the default and counts hold, but the log text is not strictly unchanged; the paraphrase overstates.

Rollback log text lives in _rollback_conversation (src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:374-465); messages are now '%s query_database call on conversation %s was not rolled back: ...' with a reason prefix. The only tests asserting rollback log text are tests/unit/test_query_database_queue.py:581-660. They key on 'was not rolled back' (message formatted as '... was not rolled back: ...'), 'raised from truncate_messages', store class names, 'belongs to a different user' (level ERROR) and the absence of 'nothing to roll back'. All substrings are still present in the current format strings (the default reason='cancelled' just prefixes the line). No other tests assert on rollback log text (grep of tests/).
